first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ while onboarding completion dropped only 4%, suggesting the decay occurs post-signup. memory_91 directly addresses week-one engagement through in-product activation messaging. Verifying memory_86 (onboarding simplification) and memory_91 (activation messaging) will clarify whether the problem is signup friction (resolved) or post-signup disengagement (unresolved). Given we can run exactly one experiment, activation_messaging targets the larger signal—engagement drop vs. completion drop—and carries lower risk than promotional_pricing (memory_73 showed retention harm) or referral_incentives (best suited for established customers, not acquisition pressure). Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB competitive threat. A standard_experiment on activation_messaging preserves the option to pivot if data refute the hypothesis, and aligns with sustainable revenue (engagement-driven, not discounting-driven).
